Let \(R\) be the radius, and let \(\theta\) be the smaller central angle between two points. Their chord distance is

\[
2R\sin(\theta/2).
\]

The condition that this distance is less than \(R\) gives

\[
2R\sin(\theta/2)<R
\iff \sin(\theta/2)<\frac12
\iff \theta<\frac{\pi}{3}.
\]

So every pair of points must have angular separation less than \(L=\pi/3\).

Fix one point \(A\) at angle \(0\). The other two points \(B,C\) are independent uniform angles. For \(A\) to be within distance \(R\) of both \(B\) and \(C\), both must lie within \(\pi/3\) of \(0\), an interval of length \(2\pi/3\). This has probability

\[
\left(\frac{2\pi/3}{2\pi}\right)^2=\left(\frac13\right)^2=\frac19.
\]

Given that \(B,C\in(-\pi/3,\pi/3)\), the distance between \(B\) and \(C\) is less than \(R\) iff their angular separation is less than \(\pi/3\). In the square \((-\pi/3,\pi/3)^2\), the region where \(|B-C|<\pi/3\) has area \(3/4\) of the square, so the conditional probability is \(3/4\).

Thus

\[
P=\frac19\cdot \frac34=\frac{1}{12}.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac{1}{12}}\).
